chapter: Bird's world, singers and the new music
title: Singers: Pha Terrell, June Richmond, Billy Eckstine

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: From that night, we went on up to.... Let's see, where did we head for. Oh, Down South, way down there in the bottom land, which I don't like to talk about, because I get angry when I think about it, you know. But we had a good time. We had a nice time. Where were we going before we got to that?
Well, we were talking about Billie Holiday and we were talking about...
How did I get off of her?
I don't know. But now that we're on singers, what other singers have you worked with who were memorable to you?

Well, Pha Terrell I liked a lot. I thought the world of him, because he sang so pretty, man, you know. It ain't every day that you run across a guy that can really sing, sing pretty. And everybody loved him. But Pha was one of those kind of guys... And when I joined the band, he wasn't with the band, but he came back with the band shortly afterwards, after I was there. Andy had Pha Terrell and Jim
McGhee (12/6) - 34
Richmond. Boy, if that don't break up the house, I don't know what will. So anyway, that's how I got to know him, through Andy's band.

He was something else, boy. People used to just throw money on the dance floor for this cat. And we had a valet who used to take a brook and just sweep up the money. Because that's what they'd do. They would just throw like five- and ten-dollar bills out there on the dance floor. "Yeah, Pha!" And he would sing "Until The Real Thing Comes Along" or "What Will I Tell My Heart" or something.
He had a fantastic voice, man. He didn't need no microphone, no nothin'. He just sang, man, and everybody would listen. He was something else.
June Richmond, she needed a mike, but yet she could holler, oh boy, like somebody had stuck something in her or something. She was something else. A lot of fun. June and I had a ball together.
Then of course, you worked with B.

Oh yeah, I just loved B's singing. I was crazy about Billy Eckstine's voice. I thought that... By working in his band, I really got to hear him that the average person wouldn't hear. I got to hear him when he didn't feel good and he had to go out there and break it up. I heard him do it -- and seen him do it. But those things
McGhee (12/6) - 35
have to happen. If you've got it, you've got it, and ain't nothin' supposed to stop you. But Billy Eckstine had a voice that was something else, too, man.

Of course, he always said that he didn't like to sing the Blues. It's just that he made that hit with "Jelly, Jelly" with Hines, and then forever after he had to sing the Blues. But he really was a ballad singer and that's what he preferred to sing.
That's what he preferred to sing, but I mean, he could sing anything. The Blues... "Jumpin' the Blues" -- you hear him sing that?
"Blowing The Blues Away."
Yeah...
"Lonesome Lover Blues."
Yeah. He sang the shit out of the Blues. He ain't no Blues singer. I'd say, "Man, you ain't, huh?" Billy was something else.
